decisions.summary: each FR-004 commit group split by class into a moves-work arm and a removes-work arm, moves-work first, each arm's revert a patch against HEAD timed by make perf-ab; reverted where its revert costs no time beyond the spread and its growth with size does not argue for it, kept otherwise, evidence in research.md
decisions.why: Departs from the spec's wording (FR-004 times 'each group's revert'), recorded here so it is not silent: the arm is a finer unit than the commit group, excludes no hunk from timing, and stops a removes-work gain in one commit from shielding a moves-work change in the same commit that bought nothing, which is the GM's 'reverting some of the changes ... that reduced call counts without actually improving performance'. 'No time beyond the spread' is a reading of FR-004's 'its time shows a gain', and the decision is judgment on evidence, not a refusal on a time (FR-006). It serves FR-004's purpose rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: a removes-work arm whose revert cannot be written against HEAD (later work built on it) is recorded so, with why, and kept
decisions.why: FR-004 says the class 'excludes no hunk from timing'; this sentence excludes a class of hunks from timing and keeps them. Its reason, 'later work built on it', is that the revert needs more of the codebase changed: such a revert can still be written, with the dependent later code adapted, and timed. It is harder, not impossible. The plan's own red exit (item 6 of every task approach) sends 'a claim that it cannot be done' through make arbiter-ask, and this sentence rules on that claim itself, bypassing the arbiter. It also covers removes-work arms only and says nothing about a moves-work arm in the same position, with no reason given for the split. The GM asked for the reverts with no carve-out. Fix: delete the sentence, or replace it with: an arm whose revert needs later work adapted is written with that work adapted and timed; a claim that it cannot be written at all goes through make arbiter-ask.

decisions.summary: Each commit group is split by hunk class into a moves-work arm and a removes-work arm, each arm's revert timed against HEAD by perf-ab; reverted where its revert costs no time beyond the spread and growth with size does not argue for it.
decisions.why: A departure in unit from FR-004/SC-003's wording ('each group's revert is timed', 'each commit group's A/B'): a two-class group gets two arm A/Bs and no single whole-group A/B. Judged within, not missed: every hunk is still timed (FR-004 'excludes no hunk from timing'), the class still orders the work moves-work first, the keep/revert rule is FR-004's own (gain or growth argues -> keep, otherwise revert), and the finer unit serves the GM's purpose at least as well - a moves-work arm that buys no time is exactly the trap the GM named ('combining multiple functions into a single function ... is pointless') and would survive a whole-group A/B carried by a removes-work gain. It shrinks nothing the GM asked to have reverted. A group with one class has one arm, i.e. the group itself.
